project_rules: Develop an outward-looking cinematic documentary idea grounded in real people, places, activities, memories, and experiences.
Let observable action, natural sound, and an independent human story carry the film; keep philosophy underneath rather than making a lecture.
Never invent participants, quotations, events, access, evidence, or outcomes.
Do not force people to illustrate doctrine and do not infer private mental states from images alone.

authorized: Refine IDEA-P01-A as an unnumbered candidate idea.
Sharpen its premise, human question, observable action, independent stakes, ethical limits, and research questions.
Label every proposed real-world lead as unverified.
forbidden: Select or suggest a named location.
Allocate an episode or release number.
Assign a chronological group or object.
Claim approval or verified facts without evidence.

idea.premise: Follow one person or a small working group through a real, bounded task that demands repeated noticing, recognition, adjustment, and care. The task—not a philosophical lesson—supplies the story: something must be made, repaired, prepared, moved, or completed, and reality decides whether it succeeds. Close observation attends to contact with materials and people, moments that feel easy, painful, or ordinary, the features workers recognize, and the choices that redirect the work. The film never claims to see inside a mind; actions, natural sound, and participants’ own words carry what can be known.
idea.central_human_question: When real work changes from moment to moment, how does a person recognize what is happening, live with how it feels, and decide what to do next?

concept_connections.title: සර්ව චිත්ත සාධාරණ චෛතසික සත
concept_connections.reason: The seven co-present functions can sharpen editorial attention to contact, feeling tone, recognition, intention, holding to an aspect, momentary maintenance, and directing the mind.
concept_connections.guardrail: Do not turn the functions into a seven-step plot or diagnose them on camera.

concept_connections.title: වේදනා සංග්‍ර‍හය
concept_connections.reason: Its pleasant, painful, and neutral distinction, plus its separation of bodily and mental forms, can make questions about experience more precise.
concept_connections.guardrail: Do not equate වේදනා with every emotion or attribute a feeling without the participant’s account.

deliberately_not_connected.reason: Do not add it merely because it is part of the pilot.

unverified_people_or_situations: A person or small team performing a skilled task with a visible beginning, constraints, corrections, and finish.
A task where touch, sound, timing, repetition, fatigue, uncertainty, and learned recognition arise naturally rather than through staging.
A participant willing to describe concrete moments without being asked to endorse the source framework.
idea.verification_note: No person, access arrangement, task, or event has been found or confirmed.
observable_material: Hands, tools, materials, faces, pauses, repeated attempts, checks, corrections, and cooperation.
The full natural-sound texture of work.
Participant explanations tied to concrete actions: what they noticed, recognized, expected, or changed.
idea.observation_guardrail: Facial expression alone is not evidence of a feeling or intention.
idea.movement_and_stakes: A real requirement, limited material or time, an error, changing conditions, or responsibility to another person could move the story only if research verifies it. Stakes must come from what completion or failure means to the participant, not from manufactured urgency.
idea.possible_viewer_movement: The viewer may begin by seeing only a finished product or routine action and come to notice the many adjustments involved. Do not pre-write mastery, personal transformation, success, or failure; the observed outcome remains unknown.
location_requirements: An active, ethically filmable working environment.
A bounded task with observable development.
Safe camera access, informed consent, and minimal disruption.
idea.location_note: No named location is proposed, selected_location_id is null, and selection remains Chathura’s alone.
idea.why_it_may_deserve_a_film: The independent story is consequential work and the relationships and judgment it requires. The film must remain worthwhile if no source terminology is spoken. C020 and C032 are editorial lenses, not the subject’s assigned beliefs.
idea.link_to_other_idea: IDEA-P01-B asks how shared names organize action, while this idea watches a person adjust within a changing task. A possible contrast is immediate experience versus meaning already attached to a situation; keep the films independent.
revise_or_abandon_if: There is no independent human stake beyond illustrating concepts.
Access requires staging action or disrupting livelihoods.
Inner experience can only be inferred from images, or participants do not want it discussed.
The activity has no real development, relationship, or consequence.
The combined framework distorts how participants understand their work.

C032.scope: මෙහි වේදනා යනු සියලු හැඟීම් එකතුව නොව, අරමුණේ රසය විඳින චෛතසික කාර්යයයි.
C032.threefold: අනුභවන භේදයෙන් සැප, දුක් සහ උපෙක්ඛා යන තුනකි. උපෙක්ඛා මෙහි සැපත් දුක්ත් නොවන මධ්‍යස්ථ විඳීමයි.
C032.fivefold: ඉන්ද්‍රිය භේදයෙන් ශාරීරික සැප, මානසික සතුට, ශාරීරික දුක්, මානසික අසතුට සහ උපෙක්ඛා යන පහකි. මෙය තුනට විරුද්ධ වර්ගීකරණයක් නොව, සැප හා දුක් ශරීර/මනස ලෙස වෙන් කිරීමකි.
C032.broader_dukkha_note: Pradeepika හි පුළුල් දුක්ඛ විග්‍රහය වෙනස්වීම හා ප්‍රත්‍යයතාව අදාළ දාර්ශනික භාවිතයක් වන අතර සියල්ල ශාරීරිකව වේදනාකාරී යන අදහස නොවේ.

english_human_interpretations.C020: Meeting a situation involves more than attention. Something makes contact with experience; it has a pleasant, painful, or neutral tone; features are recognized; activity is organized; the mind holds to some aspect; the moment is sustained; and the mind is directed. The source presents these together, not as a universal seven-stage sequence. Using them to choose interview questions or notice edits is an editorial application; a camera cannot prove seven hidden mental factors. The source meanings of intention/karma and mental life faculty do not transfer fully into ordinary English without context.
english_human_interpretations.C032: An experience can feel pleasant, painful, or neither, with the source also distinguishing bodily from mental forms. This is not a list of every emotion. A film may ask what feels easy, painful, unwelcome, or ordinary and how that may influence a response, but it must not claim a universal chain or scientific validation. The participant’s account and observable context are evidence; an edit or expression is not enough. The source’s broader dukkha account cannot be reduced to everything feels bad.
